title: Intent recognition
evidenceStatus: 785 completed sampled official test cases, including 69 recovered transport failures; full distributions and request text preserved
summary: The experiment uses all 77 BANKING77 or 151 CLINC candidate labels, but the page hides its trained baseline and out-of-scope breakdown. Full official tests require only 8,580 intent decisions, compared with the current 785; label definitions and validation-only rejection thresholds would make the comparison more useful.
strengths: Every recorded benchmark case is complete and includes full request text and all candidate probabilities.
The baseline trains on the official training split and predictions are paired by source ID.
Recovery preserves completed mistakes and separates provider outages from semantic errors.
Pinned sources, provenance links, content notices, calibration diagnostics, and paired bootstrap values already exist.

findings.title: The page hides its baseline and the source of the CLINC gain
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/benchmarks.tsx:265 does not render tfidf_logistic, baseline_rows, or paired_difference. Current records show BANKING77 314/385 versus baseline 343/385; CLINC in scope 271/300 versus 269/300 and OOS 83/100 versus 13/100. README.md:31 still describes initial-run values.
findings.impact: Visitors cannot assess whether Jev is useful or distinguish OOS gains from known-intent accuracy.
findings.fix: Show both systems, baseline predictions, disagreement filters, paired intervals, and separate in-scope/OOS scores; generate narrative tables from current data.

findings.title: Sampled coverage leaves feasible official test cases unmeasured
findings.evidence: src/jev_lab/benchmarks.py:42 samples five BANKING77 and two CLINC cases per known intent. Pinned source counts are 3,080 BANKING77 and 5,500 CLINC/OOS test cases. Current 385 and 400 cases cover 12.50% and 7.27%.
findings.impact: Class-level results from two CLINC cases are unstable, and the sample changes OOS prevalence from 18.18% to 25%.
findings.fix: Run all official test IDs with frozen prompts, complete candidate sets, resumable recording, and dataset-specific completion counts. Preserve the sampled run as historical evidence.

findings.title: OOS comparison omits a validation-selected rejection baseline
findings.evidence: src/jev_lab/benchmarks.py:48 uses a plain 151-way logistic argmax; no validation threshold is fitted. Jev falsely rejects 8/300 supported requests and routes 17/100 unsupported requests. Ten wrong predictions across datasets carry probability exactly 1.
findings.impact: The current OOS advantage is against one weak operating point, and raw probability is easy to mistake for reliable confidence.
findings.fix: Fit thresholds only on validation; show OOS recall/precision, supported false rejection, accepted accuracy, and coverage. Preserve raw distributions and distinguish exploratory test sliders from frozen benchmark thresholds.

findings.title: Bare label names underspecify fine-grained intent distinctions
findings.evidence: src/jev_lab/data.py:68 and :82 replace underscores with spaces. experience-prototypes/results/classify.jsonl:1215 records transactions versus spending_history confusion at predicted probability 1.
findings.impact: The current condition measures matching against label names; visitors cannot understand the ontology boundary or all candidates.
findings.fix: Preserve the raw-label condition; add a frozen training-derived description condition and a searchable drawer of all definitions, instructions, and training-only examples. Do not tune descriptions on observed test errors.

findings.title: Per-case source links and recovery counts use the wrong dataset context
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/scripts/enrich.py:45 sets a BANKING77-only source_url; src/benchmarks.tsx:252 renders it for CLINC. src/benchmarks.tsx:327 passes the combined recovery object, reporting 69 recoveries instead of per-dataset 43 or 26.
findings.impact: Provenance and availability details become misleading when the visitor switches datasets.
findings.fix: Store and render dataset-specific source URL, split size, sampling rule, recovery count, and run metadata. Bind future content notices to stable case IDs.

simulation.title: A support desk that knows when to ask
simulation.description: An animated inbox shows the same request moving through Jev and baseline lanes into predefined support routes. Visitors inspect route definitions, compare disagreements, preview rejection thresholds, and try scripted clarifications.
simulation.jevsRole: Classify the complete request and, in a separately evaluated interaction condition, choose a bounded clarification question when supported intents remain ambiguous.
simulation.codeRole: Validate intent IDs, apply a frozen acceptance policy, version requests, cancel stale responses, animate the inbox, and render route outcomes.
acceptanceCriteria: Expose the actual prompt and every candidate description.
Both lanes consume identical request text and show the corresponding downstream route.
A threshold preview shows coverage, mistakes, and unsupported false routes without changing the frozen benchmark result.
Transport failures remain waiting states; semantic mistakes remain visible.
Keyboard, reduced motion, cancellation, and request-version checks work.

evaluation.design: Freeze one canonical prompt and candidate set, then run all 8,580 official test cases with one request and one decision per case. CLINC reports official in-scope accuracy and OOS recall, with precision/false rejection as additional measures. Add 3,100 CLINC validation and 1,001 BANKING77 train-held-out calibration decisions for a total 12,681-decision calibrated protocol. Separate the full-training baseline from a calibrated baseline trained on the remaining 9,002 BANKING77 examples. A three-permutation order audit on the existing 785 sampled IDs adds 2,355 decisions. Bootstrap paired utterances, not retries or permutations. Separately evaluate 120 authored support-desk cases across three presentation seeds.
baselines: Current full-training TF-IDF logistic regression, clearly labeled supervised.
TF-IDF logistic regression with validation-selected OOS rejection.
For the simulation: direct argmax and fixed-threshold routing versus clarification.
metrics: BANKING77 exact label accuracy and macro-F1
CLINC in-scope accuracy and OOS recall
OOS precision and supported-request false rejection
Accepted accuracy at frozen coverage and risk-coverage curves
Paired bootstrap differences and Wilson intervals for binary rates
Calibration diagnostics retaining raw rounded distributions
Simulation final-route correctness, clarification count, unresolved rate, and elapsed interaction time

coverage.current: 385 BANKING77 cases plus 300 CLINC in-scope and 100 OOS cases, all completed. Five separate authored semantic requests are excluded from these benchmark counts.
coverage.full: 3,080 BANKING77 + 4,500 CLINC in-scope + 1,000 CLINC OOS = 8,580 cases and 1,067,660 candidate-option scores.
coverage.feasibility: Feasible with the existing all-label runner: 8,580 fresh logical requests or 7,795 missing-case requests if the original request condition is retained. No large-model or dataset-size blocker; needs resumable transport, complete manifests, OOS calibration, and scalable exploration.
